instruction: I have a spreadsheet with research papers on my desktop. Find which paper has the most authors and save the paper title to a text file named "most_authors.txt" in the /home/user directory.

metadata.explanation: Verified with Python: TinyBERT and Attention Is All You Need both have 8 authors (tied for most). TinyBERT appears first in the list. Evaluator accepts either title.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies the instruction: checks if the saved text file contains one of the two valid paper titles (both tied with 8 authors)
Metric logic correctly implements OR condition: uses 'any()' to return 1.0 if ANY valid title is present, which appropriately handles multiple correct answers
Expected values complete and correct: includes both 'TinyBERT' and 'Attention Is All You Need' which are verified (per metadata) to both have 8 authors
Getter logic correct: reads text file content from the specified path '/home/user/most_authors.txt'
Case-insensitive matching implemented: uses .lower() for robust comparison, avoiding false negatives due to capitalization
Substring matching is semantically appropriate: allows flexibility for users who might write additional context like 'The paper with most authors is: TinyBERT'
Data flow semantically correct: file content → substring check → returns 1.0 for correct answer, 0.0 for incorrect
